codeReview.summary: Clean implementation of both MQTT command rate limiting and OTA URL scheme validation. The RateLimiter struct uses a simple windowed counter (10 commands per 10-second window) with proper window reset logic. URL validation correctly requires http:// and rejects all other schemes with appropriate logging. Integration into the command dispatch in main.rs is correct — only Command variants are rate-limited, not pump timers, which is a reasonable design choice. Code follows existing patterns, is well-documented with comments, and compiles cleanly.

issues.description: RateLimiter uses a fixed-window approach (resets counter completely on window expiry) rather than a sliding-window. This means at the boundary of a window, you could get 20 commands in rapid succession (10 at end of window N, 10 at start of window N+1). This is acceptable for protecting the spa bus (the purpose is to prevent flooding, not guarantee strict rate), but worth noting as a design trade-off.

The URL scheme validation uses a heuristic `url.find(':').map_or(false, |i| i < 8)` to detect schemes like 'data:...' without '://'. The magic number 8 could be fragile if new short scheme names appear, but in practice this covers the known cases (data:, mailto:, tel:) well and the OTA URL context makes exotic schemes extremely unlikely.

summary: Feature passes review. Both MQTT command rate limiting (10 commands per 10-second window) and OTA URL scheme validation (http:// only) are correctly implemented. Rate limiting uses a clean RateLimiter struct integrated into the command dispatch path in main.rs. URL validation properly rejects file://, ftp://, https://, data:, and schemeless URLs with warn! logging. Pump timers are correctly exempted from rate limiting. No unit tests were added, which is expected since the code lives in the esp-hal-dependent app/ crate. Two minor non-blocking observations: the fixed-window approach allows brief bursts at window boundaries, and the URL scheme detection uses a heuristic magic number (8). Both are acceptable for the use case.
